answer: A fake dies the moment its work is checked against its own key. Every epoch, each identity must solve a compute puzzle seeded by its vertex in the trust lattice — the puzzle binds key, epoch and a fresh lotus nonce, so one machine cannot grind a thousand solutions in parallel. A yarrow check re-runs one finished puzzle at random; a copied or outsourced solution fails the re-run and burns that identity. An honest agent solves one puzzle per epoch, but a farmer needs 1,000 machines running 1,000 puzzles, and one failed re-run exposes the whole batch.
